content:--- coscribe: doc --- # Q3 2026 Sales Review Q3 closed at $13,375,000 of revenue against a $23,300,000 target — 57.4% attainment and 37.2% below Q2's $21,300,000. Gross profit was $4,798,139 at a 35.9% margin. No region came within 33 points of its target, so this is a quarter-wide miss rather than one territory's problem. ## The quarter at a glance | Region | Revenue | Q3 target | Attainment | vs Q2 | Gross profit | GM% | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | South | 2,554,000 | 3,800,000 | 67.2% | −39.2% | 975,251 | 38.2% | | North | 3,107,000 | 4,900,000 | 63.4% | −29.4% | 1,057,906 | 34.1% | | East | 2,814,000 | 4,600,000 | 61.2% | −41.4% | 1,010,625 | 35.9% | | Southwest | 2,715,000 | 5,500,000 | 49.4% | −38.3% | 944,774 | 34.8% | | Central | 2,185,000 | 4,500,000 | 48.6% | −37.6% | 809,583 | 37.1% | | **Total** | **13,375,000** | **23,300,000** | **57.4%** | **−37.2%** | **4,798,139** | **35.9%** | Revenue fell evenly through the quarter — 4,569,000 in July, 4,523,000 in August, 4,283,000 in September — so there was no single bad month to point at, and no recovery in the final month either. ## Revenue against target by region ```chart bar Q3 revenue vs target by region | Region | Q3 target | Q3 revenue | | --- | --- | --- | | South | 3800000 | 2554000 | | North | 4900000 | 3107000 | | East | 4600000 | 2814000 | | Southwest | 5500000 | 2715000 | | Central | 4500000 | 2185000 | ``` South was the strongest performer in rate terms (67.2%) and also carried the best margin, but its target was the smallest of the five. The two largest absolute gaps sit in **Southwest** (−$2,785,000) and **Central** (−$2,315,000) — between them $5.1M, more than a third of the total shortfall of $9,925,000. Southwest is the standout: it was given the biggest target of the quarter, $1.1M above its Q2 actual, and delivered 49.4% of it. Attainment and Q2 comparison disagree in one place worth noting: North fell least against Q2 (−29.4%) but still only reached 63.4% of target, because its target was raised from $4.4M to $4.9M. Southwest's target was raised further still, by the same $1.1M. ## Margin held, but not everywhere The 35.9% blended margin is close to where a quarter at this mix should land, so price did not collapse with volume. Product margins are tightly packed — smart lock 37.4%, robot vacuum 35.8%, smart speaker 35.3%, security camera 35.1% — which makes the regional spread the more telling number: **North at 34.1%** against **South at 38.2%**, a 4.1-point gap on comparable product mix. Where margin went thin, it went thin on large orders. The five lowest-margin lines of the quarter were all above $200,000 of revenue: | Month | Region | Product | Customer | Revenue | GM% | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Sep | North | Robot vacuum | Cedar Property | 237,000 | 26.4% | | Sep | North | Smart speaker | Swift Logistics | 359,000 | 26.7% | | Sep | East | Security camera | Northwind Homes | 202,000 | 26.7% | | Aug | Central | Robot vacuum | Swift Logistics | 363,000 | 27.6% | | Jul | Southwest | Security camera | Lumen Tech | 206,000 | 27.7% | Three of the five are September deals, which suggests quarter-end discounting rather than a structural cost problem. ## Customer concentration Swift Logistics was the largest account at $2,524,000 — 18.9% of revenue — and the thinnest of the major accounts at 32.4% gross margin, four to eight points below Oakline Living (37.7%) and Bluepeak Electronics (40.6%). It appears in both the margin table above and the top of the revenue table. Harbor Retail ($2,050,000, 33.8%) and Cedar Property ($1,423,000, 33.2%) show the same pattern in milder form. ## Next steps 1. **Rebase or re-explain the plan.** Confirm whether the $23.3M target reflected real pipeline or was set from prior-year growth, and agree a Q4 number that the current run rate supports. Owner: [finance lead], by [date]. 2. **Take Southwest apart.** It carried the biggest target and the biggest gap. Break its $2,785,000 shortfall into lost deals, slipped deals and deals that never entered the funnel, and decide whether the $5.5M target or the coverage behind it was the problem. Owner: [Southwest regional lead], by [date]. 3. **Fix Central's volume, not its price.** Central's margin (37.1%) is second-best in the company; its problem is that it generated the least revenue of any region on the second-largest target. This is a demand-generation and coverage question. 4. **Stop the quarter-end discount.** Set a floor margin by product and a deal-desk review for anything above $200,000 that prices below 30%, since that is where the leakage concentrates. 5. **Renegotiate the Swift Logistics terms.** Nearly a fifth of revenue at the lowest major-account margin is the single largest exposure in the book — either the volume justifies a repriced contract or the mix needs rebalancing toward Oakline Living and Bluepeak. 6. **Report weekly through Q4.** Monthly reporting was too slow to catch a three-month slide; a weekly revenue-and-margin view per region, reviewed against the rebased plan, closes that gap. Owner: [sales ops], from [date].
